title: Arsenal End 22-Year Premier League Drought as City Stumble at Bournemouth
excerpt: Mikel Arteta’s defensive juggernaut clinches a 14th English league title — and Indian fans from Mumbai to Manhattan celebrated into the night
body:
Arsenal are Premier League champions for the first time since the Arsène Wenger era, after Manchester City's 1-1 draw at Bournemouth on Tuesday confirmed that the Gunners' five-point lead at the top of the table had become unassailable.

## The Long Road Back

The wait stretched 22 years — from the 2003-04 Invincibles to a squad rebuilt from scratch by Mikel Arteta, who took charge of a directionless Arsenal in December 2019 and spent half a decade turning them into the most formidable defensive unit in English football. This season, Arsenal posted 19 clean sheets in 37 league matches, scored 24 goals from set pieces (breaking Manchester United's 2012-13 record of 23), and ground out result after result even when the football was more steel than silk.

Viktor Gyökeres, the Swedish striker signed from Sporting CP for €63.5 million last summer, contributed 14 league goals and gave Arsenal the physical presence they had lacked in three consecutive runner-up finishes. But this title was won by collective discipline: Jurrien Timber's defensive marshalling, Bukayo Saka's creative menace, and Martin Ødegaard's metronomic passing from midfield all proved essential.

Arsenal's coronation came without them kicking a ball on Tuesday evening. Having beaten Burnley 1-0 on Monday to extend their lead to five points with 82, they simply needed City to drop points. Pep Guardiola's side drew 1-1, and the result left City stuck on a maximum of 81 points.

## Arteta's Pragmatic Revolution

Critics will note that Arsenal's title was won on pragmatism rather than panache. The set-piece obsession, the willingness to defend deep leads, and a reliance on dead-ball situations over open-play brilliance drew comparisons to José Mourinho's most effective sides. Arteta has been unapologetic: "I asked myself what we needed to do to win this league, not what we needed to do to look beautiful," he said after the Burnley victory.

The numbers support his approach. Arsenal conceded just 28 goals all season, the fewest in the division, and their expected goals against per match was the lowest in Europe's top five leagues. Three successive second-place finishes had taught Arteta that talent alone was not enough to dethrone a City side that had won six of the last seven titles.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

The Premier League's hold on the Indian sporting imagination is enormous — an estimated 150 million viewers tune in across the subcontinent each season, and the league's fan clubs have chapters in every major Indian city. Arsenal's global fanbase is among the league's largest, with active supporters' groups from Delhi to Dubai to the Bay Area.

For NRI fans who have endured two decades of near-misses, the celebrations were real: social media lit up with watch-party clips from living rooms in New Jersey, pubs in London's Southall, and cafés in Bengaluru. In the United States, the match aired on USA Network and Peacock; in India, Star Sports and JioHotstar carried the broadcast.

The timing is poignant. Many of the diaspora's millennial Arsenal supporters grew up idolising Thierry Henry and Patrick Vieira during the last title-winning era, then watched through years of austerity, stadium-debt repayments, and competitive mediocrity. This new title feels like vindication for a fanbase that stayed loyal through the banter years.

## What's Next

Arsenal travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday to collect the trophy — a rare away-day coronation — before turning their attention to the UEFA Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on May 30. A league-and-European double would mark the most successful season in the club's history, surpassing even the Invincibles campaign.

For Arteta, the 44-year-old Basque who once played under Wenger and now sits alongside him in Arsenal's pantheon, the message is clear: this is only the beginning.
